  "claim": "recover_json_object ignores a fenced JSON object with duplicate keys as a fenced candidate, so it can fall through to a later top-level object instead of scoring the fenced object.",
  "expected": "For content containing a fenced object with duplicate keys followed by a later top-level object, recover_json_object returns the fenced object resolved last-wins (e.g. {'a': 2}) because the doc says a candidate with repeated keys resolved last-wins is scoreable and the last fenced object has priority.",
  "observed": "The code skips the fenced candidate when strict parsing fails (it only applies _loads_last_wins to the top_level pool), then scans top_level and returns the later strict object {'b': 3}.",
  "reproducer": "```json\\n{\\\"a\\\": 1, \\\"a\\\": 2}\\n```\\n{\\\"b\\\": 3}",
  "source_basis": "\"The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one, else the last top-level object in the text\" and \"A candidate that parses as strict JSON, or as JSON with repeated keys resolved last-wins, is scoreable\".",
  "execution_evidence": "none: no executable oracle",
  "scope": "Replies containing a fenced JSON object with duplicate keys and at least one later top-level JSON object outside the fence.",
  "uncertainty": "I could not run the code; the reasoning assumes json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode accepts duplicate keys and includes fenced objects in the top_level pool, which is standard Python behaviour."
}
